original_question: For random-matrix models that depend on external parameters p and undergo critical changes in the support of the equilibrium measure at values p_c, can one rigorously analyze the corresponding double-scaling and more general multi-scaling limits in which p approaches p_c while the matrix size n tends to infinity?
target_in_paper: Problem 2 (universality for random matrix theory (RMT)), specifically the unnumbered open problem near the end of the discussion on support transitions and critical behavior: Deift asks for rigorous analysis of double-scaling problems p -> p_c with n -> infinity, and more generally multi-scaling limits, for parameter-dependent matrix distributions whose equilibrium measures change at critical values p_c. ([m.mathnet.ru](https://m.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=sigma&option_lang=eng&paperid=1216&what=fullt))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly keeps the setting in random matrix theory, includes external parameters p, critical values p_c, changes in the equilibrium measure, the simultaneous limit p -> p_c with n -> infinity, and the paper's emphasis on double-scaling and more general multi-scaling limits. ([m.mathnet.ru](https://m.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=sigma&option_lang=eng&paperid=1216&what=fullt))
missing_details: The paper phrases the setup as matrix distributions depending on external parameter(s) p, rather than arbitrary random-matrix models in an unspecified sense. ([m.mathnet.ru](https://m.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=sigma&option_lang=eng&paperid=1216&what=fullt))

The critical event is stated as a change in the nature of the equilibrium measure; changes in support such as intervals opening, closing, or merging are motivating examples from the nearby context, but 'support change' is slightly narrower than the paper's wording. ([m.mathnet.ru](https://m.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=sigma&option_lang=eng&paperid=1216&what=fullt))
The asymptotic variable n is the size of the n x n matrices. ([m.mathnet.ru](https://m.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=sigma&option_lang=eng&paperid=1216&what=fullt))

The nearby example is the unitary invariant ensemble with density proportional to exp(-n tr V(M)) dM, where V(x) = -a x^2 + b x^4 with b > 0 fixed and a in R; there is a critical value a_c at which the equilibrium measure changes from one interval to two, and at a = a_c the two intervals merge at a critical point x_c. This example motivates the general problem but is not itself the full official statement. ([m.mathnet.ru](https://m.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=sigma&option_lang=eng&paperid=1216&what=fullt))

The paper does not specify a particular scaling exponent, rate relation between p - p_c and n, class of observables, or a prescribed limiting Painleve object in the general formulation, so adding such specifics would go beyond the statement actually posed. ([m.mathnet.ru](https://m.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=sigma&option_lang=eng&paperid=1216&what=fullt))

The paper explicitly treats this as an open problem and says that most such double-scaling problems remain open. ([m.mathnet.ru](https://m.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=sigma&option_lang=eng&paperid=1216&what=fullt))

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, operator-definition, or nilpotency condition is part of this formulation; importing such algebraic data would not be faithful to the paper. ([m.mathnet.ru](https://m.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=sigma&option_lang=eng&paperid=1216&what=fullt))
refined_question: In random matrix theory, for n x n matrix distributions depending on external parameter(s) p and having critical values p_c at which the associated equilibrium measure changes its nature—for example, when intervals in its support open, close, or merge—can one rigorously analyze the corresponding double-scaling limits in which p -> p_c as n -> infinity, and more generally the analogous multi-scaling limits? ([m.mathnet.ru](https://m.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=sigma&option_lang=eng&paperid=1216&what=fullt))
justification: This rewrite stays closest to the paper's actual intent because it tracks the final general formulation in Problem 2 rather than over-specializing either to the quartic example or to Wigner ensembles alone. It adds only the nearby context needed to make the question stand-alone: the ensembles are n x n, the parameters enter through the matrix distribution, and criticality concerns a change in the equilibrium measure, with support-opening/closing/merging as the motivating mechanism. It also avoids adding scaling exponents, observables, or extra hypotheses that Deift does not specify in the open problem itself. ([m.mathnet.ru](https://m.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=sigma&option_lang=eng&paperid=1216&what=fullt))
